extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies) preparing SEC proxy and registration statement executive/director compensation disclosures; corporate counsel, corporate secretaries, accountants, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory instructions and detailed disclosure requirements (tables, narrative, definitions, valuation and footnote rules) that registrants must follow when preparing executive officer and director compensation disclosures under Item 402 of Regulation S-K, including scaled rules for smaller reporting companies and emerging growth companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perquisites and personal benefits reporting threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded as long as the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits for a director (or named executive officer where applicable) is less than $10,000. If the total is $10,000 or more for any individual, then each perquisite or personal benefit, regardless of amount, must be identified by type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If perquisites/personal benefits required to be reported, any perquisite or benefit that exceeds the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the total perquisites for that individual must be quantified and disclosed in a footnote. Perquisites and personal benefits shall be valued on the basis of the aggregate incremental cost to the registrant; for perquisites requiring footnote quantification, describe the methodology for computing aggregate incremental cost. Reimbursements of taxes owed with respect to perquisites or benefits must be included in the appropriate tax reimbursement column and separately quantified and identified, even if the underlying perquisites themselves are below the $10,000 threshold or otherwise excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dollar value of total compensation (table total column)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dollar value of total compensation for the covered fiscal year (Director Table column (h) or Summary Compensation Table column (j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each individual, disclose the sum of all amounts reported in the applicable component columns (i.e., sum of columns (b) through (g) for directors or (c) through (i) for named executive officers in the Summary Compensation Table).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping directors with identical compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more directors may be grouped in a single row in the Director Compensation Table if all elements of their compensation are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grouped, the names of the directors for whom disclosure is presented on a group basis should be clear from the Table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative to director compensation table
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a narrative description of any material factors necessary to an understanding of the director compensation disclosed in the Director Compensation Table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material factors will vary; examples include a description of standard compensation arrangements (retainer, committee service, chairman fees, meeting attendance) and whether any director has a different compensation arrangement, identifying that director and describing its terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaled disclosure for smaller reporting and emerging growth companies
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that qualifies as a 'smaller reporting company' or as an 'emerging growth company' may provide the scaled disclosure specified in paragraphs (m) through (r) instead of the full disclosure in paragraphs (a) through (k), (s), and (u).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller reporting companies should follow the alternative (m)-(r) rules, including alternate tables and narrative requirements tailored to scaled disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: All compensation covered (smaller reporting companies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require clear, concise, and understandable disclosure of all plan and non-plan compensation awarded to, earned by, or paid to the named executive officers and directors by any person for all services rendered in all capacities to the smaller reporting company and its subsidiaries, unless specifically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes compensation furnished via third-party transactions intended to furnish compensation. Amounts reported in one fiscal year need not be reported the same way in subsequent years; treatment may differ year-to-year under this Item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons covered (named executive officers for smaller reporting companies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure must be provided for: (i) all individuals serving as the smaller reporting company's principal executive officer (PEO) during the last completed fiscal year; (ii) the two most highly compensated executive officers other than the PEO who were serving as executive officers at year-end; and (iii) up to two additional individuals who would have been included under (ii) but were not serving as executive officers at year-end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the 'named executive officers' for smaller reporting companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of most highly compensated executive officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine which executive officers are most highly compensated by reference to total compensation for the last completed fiscal year reduced by the amount required to be disclosed pursuant to paragraph (n)(2)(viii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, no disclosure need be provided for any executive officer (other than the PEO) whose reduced total compensation does not exceed $100,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of subsidiary executive officers
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be appropriate for a smaller reporting company to include as named executive officers one or more executive officers or other employees of subsidiaries in the disclosure required by this Item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 3b-7 under the Exchange Act for treatment of subsidiary officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of executive officer due to overseas compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: In limited circumstances, a smaller reporting company may exclude from disclosure an individual (other than the PEO) who would be among the most highly compensated because the executive's high compensation is due predominantly to overseas assignment-related cash compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a limited, fact-specific exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information for full fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PEO or another named executive officer served in that capacity during any part of the fiscal year for which information is required, information should be provided as to all of his or her compensation for the full fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies even if the person served only part of the fiscal year or in a different position during parts of the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of table or column if no compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: A table or column may be omitted if there has been no compensation awarded to, earned by, or paid to any of the named executive officers or directors required to be reported in that table or column in any fiscal year covered by that table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits omission where no amounts apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: stock, option, SARs, equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Stock means instruments such as common stock, restricted stock, restricted stock units, phantom stock, phantom stock units, common stock equivalent units or similar instruments without option-like features. Option means instruments such as stock options, stock appreciation rights and similar instruments with option-like features. SARs refers to SARs payable in cash or stock. Equity refers generally to stock and/or options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions when characterizing awards for disclosure and in the tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'plan' includes any plan, contract, authorization or arrangement, whether or not in a formal document, pursuant to which cash, securities, similar instruments, or any other property may be received; a plan may be applicable to one person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as to paragraph (t) disclosures, smaller reporting companies may omit information regarding group life, health, hospitalization, or medical reimbursement plans that do not discriminate in scope, terms or operation in favor of executives or directors and that are generally available to all salaried employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: incentive plan and incentive plan award (equity vs non-equity)
rubrics_metrics.description: An incentive plan provides compensation intended to serve as incentive for performance over a specified period; an equity incentive plan awards fall within FASB ASC Topic 718; a non-equity incentive plan is not an equity incentive plan. 'Incentive plan award' means an award provided under an incentive plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine reporting columns and valuation approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: date of grant and closing market price
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'date of grant' or 'grant date' refers to the grant date determined for financial reporting purposes pursuant to FASB ASC Topic 718. 'Closing market price' is the price at which the security was last sold in the principal U.S. market for such security as of the determined date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions for computing grant-date fair values and market values in tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Compensation Table required columns
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Summary Compensation Table concerning compensation of named executive officers for the last two completed fiscal years in the specified tabular format with columns: Name and principal position; Year; Salary; Bonus; Stock awards; Option awards; Nonequity incentive plan compensation; Nonqualified deferred compensation earnings; All other compensation; Total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed order and column definitions precisely when constructing the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and bonus reporting instructions for smaller reporting companies
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amount of salary or bonus earned in a given fiscal year is not calculable through the latest practicable date, include a footnote disclosing that the amount is not calculable and provide the expected determination date; such amount must be disclosed in an 8-K when later determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller reporting companies shall include in the salary or bonus columns any amount of salary or bonus forgone at the election of a named executive officer under which equity or other non-cash compensation instead has been received; disclose the receipt in a footnote added to the salary/bonus column and refer to the narrative disclosure where material terms of the award are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock and option awards reporting and valuation (ASC 718)
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards of stock, report the aggregate grant date fair value computed in accordance with FASB ASC Topic 718 (stock awards column). For awards of options (with or without tandem SARs), report the aggregate grant date fair value computed in accordance with ASC 718 (option awards column).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a footnote disclosing all valuation assumptions by reference to discussion in the registrant's financial statements or MD&A. If awards were repriced or materially modified during the year, include the incremental fair value computed as of the repricing/modification date in the option awards column. For awards subject to performance conditions, report the grant-date value based on the probable outcome; if a lesser amount than the maximum is included, footnote the value assuming the highest level of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-equity incentive plan compensation reporting (column g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the dollar value of all earnings for services performed during the fiscal year pursuant to awards under non-equity incentive plans and all earnings on any outstanding awards in the non-equity incentive plan compensation column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the relevant performance measure is satisfied during the fiscal year (even for a single year in a multi-year plan), the earnings are reportable for that fiscal year even if pay-out occurs later. All earnings on non-equity incentive plan compensation must be identified and quantified in a footnote to the column, whether paid, payable but deferred, or payable at a later date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Above-market or preferential earnings reporting (column h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report above-market or preferential earnings on compensation that is deferred on a non-tax-qualified basis (including nonqualified defined contribution plans) in the designated column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest on deferred compensation is above-market only if the rate exceeds 120% of the applicable federal long-term rate with compounding per IRC section 1274(d); calculate the above-market portion only. If interest rates vary by condition, compute assuming satisfaction of all conditions to receive the highest rate. Dividends on deferred stock are preferential only if earned at a rate higher than dividends on common stock; report only the preferential portion. Footnote or narrative may explain the registrant's criteria for determining above-market or preferential amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Other Compensation (column i) inclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All other compensation for the covered fiscal year that cannot be properly reported in other columns must be included in the 'All Other Compensation' column; each compensation item not properly reportable in other columns must be included regardless of amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: perquisites and other personal benefits or property unless aggregate < $10,000; gross-ups/tax reimbursements; compensation cost for discounted security purchases (unless discount generally available); amounts paid or accrued in connection with termination or change-in-control; contributions to defined contribution plans; life insurance premiums paid by the company for benefit of the officer; dividends or other earnings on stock/option awards when not factored into grant-date fair value. Non-equity incentive awards/earnings should not be reported here. Benefits paid under defined benefit/actuarial plans are not reportable here unless accelerated by a change-in-control. Reimbursements of taxes owed with respect to perquisites must be included as tax reimbursements even if perquisites themselves are excluded for being < $10,000. Perquisites are valued on the aggregate incremental cost; an 'accrued amount' is an amount for which payment has become due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding and currency conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: All compensation values in the Summary Compensation Table must be reported in dollars and rounded to the nearest dollar; reported numerically as a single numerical value for each grid cell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compensation was paid or received in a different currency, provide a footnote identifying the currency and describing the rate and methodology used to convert the amounts to dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director compensation reflected for dual-role individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a named executive officer is also a director who receives compensation for services as a director, reflect that compensation in the Summary Compensation Table and provide a footnote identifying and itemizing such director compensation and amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the categories in the Director Compensation Table for such director compensation (per paragraph (r)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative disclosure to Summary Compensation Table (material factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a narrative description of any material factors necessary to an understanding of the information disclosed in the Summary Compensation Table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include material terms of employment agreements; description of repricings or material modifications of outstanding equity awards (and exceptions for pre-existing formulas, antidilution, recapitalizations, etc.); waiver/modification of performance targets (identify scope and affected officers); material terms of grants (exercisability, conditions, tandem/reload/tax-reimbursement features, provisions that could lower exercise price); material terms of non-equity incentive plan awards (formula/criteria and vesting); method of calculating earnings on nonqualified deferred compensation; identification of items under All Other Compensation to the extent material. Identification is not material if the item does not exceed the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the category in question (per paragraph (n)(2)(ix)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding equity awards at fiscal year-end table requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a tabular disclosure for unexercised options, stock that has not vested, and equity incentive plan awards outstanding as of the end of the last completed fiscal year with columns for number exercisable, number unexercisable, unearned options, option exercise price, option expiration date, number of shares that have not vested, market value of shares not vested, number of unearned shares/units/rights not vested, and market/payout value of unearned shares/rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on an award-by-award basis and follow the column definitions precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding equity awards footnotes and valuation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify by footnote any award that has been transferred other than for value and disclose vesting dates by footnote. Compute market values by multiplying closing market price at fiscal-year end by the number of shares/units or amount of equity incentive awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of shares reported for awards with performance conditions should be based on achieving threshold performance goals, except if the prior fiscal year's performance exceeded threshold, use the next higher performance measure. If target amount not determinable, provide a representative amount based on prior fiscal year performance. Multiple awards may be aggregated where exercise/expiration/pricing identical. Options/stock awarded under equity incentive plans are reported in performance columns until conditions satisfied; once satisfied, move to exercisable/unexercisable or stock columns as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional narrative disclosure for smaller reporting companies (retirement/termination plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide narrative description of material terms of each plan providing retirement benefits or benefits paid primarily following retirement, and of each contract/agreement/plan/arrangement that provides for payments at, following, or in connection with resignation, retirement, termination, or change-in-control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe material terms to the extent material for each named executive officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Compensation Table required columns and items (smaller reporting companies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Director Compensation Table for the last completed fiscal year with columns: Name; Fees earned or paid in cash; Stock awards; Option awards; Non-equity incentive plan compensation; Nonqualified deferred compensation earnings; All other compensation; Total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include for each director the items specified and follow valuation/reporting rules analogous to the Summary Compensation Table. For stock and option awards, include aggregate grant-date fair value per ASC 718 and footnote aggregate numbers outstanding at fiscal year end.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Other Compensation in Director Table: items and footnote quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: All other compensation not reportable in other director table columns must be included regardless of amount and must be identified and quantified in a footnote if material per paragraph (o)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of items to include mirror those for named executive officers: perquisites (unless aggregate < $10,000), gross-ups, discounted security purchases compensation cost per ASC 718, termination/change-in-control payments, contributions to DC plans, consulting fees, director legacy program payments, life insurance premiums, dividends/earnings not factored into grant-date fair value. For charity/legacy programs, provide footnote disclosure of total dollar amount payable and material terms when tabular disclosure provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative to director compensation table (additional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide narrative description of any material factors necessary to an understanding of the director compensation disclosed in the Director Compensation Table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include standard compensation arrangements (retainer, committee service, chairman fees, meeting attendance) and identification and description of any director with a different compensation arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions and cross-references applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions to the smaller reporting company director and summary tables indicate applicability of various instructions across analogous columns and disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many instructions to paragraph (c) and (n) apply equally to paragraph (r), and cross-references should be followed to apply analogous valuation, rounding, footnote, and materiality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation policies and practices risk disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If risks arising from the registrant's compensation policies and practices for its employees are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on the registrant, discuss the registrant's policies and practices of compensating its employees (including non-executive officers) as they relate to risk management practices and risk-taking incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrative disclosure should explain how compensation design and practices create or mitigate material risks to the company.
